title: Fix HISAT2 double-chr prefix in downstream parsers (0% REDIportal artifact)
description: Downstream parsers BCFtools.py:60-61, REDItools2.py:35, SPRINT.py:36 unconditionally prepend 'chr' for the hisat2 aligner (line[0]='chr'+line[0]). HISAT2 was aligned to a chr-prefixed reference, so raw beds already have chr1 -> becomes chrchr1 -> zero overlap with REDIportal/Alu/HEK293T DB. Result: every HISAT2 REDIportal/Alu/SNP column is artificially 0 for BCFTools, REDItools2/3, SPRINT. Proof: RED-ML/JACUSA2 parsers lack this line and report correct nonzero HISAT2 numbers. Fix via the runtime patcher in rules/morales_downstream.smk: make the prepend idempotent (only prepend when not already startswith chr). Keep submodule pristine.
close_reason: Fixed: HISAT2 idempotent chr-prepend + JACUSA2 dropna(how=all)+fillna via runtime patcher; JACUSA2 gated on config jacusa2_comparison (skip when absent). title: Patch REDItools2 complement_map to handle IUPAC ambiguity codes
description:
REDItools2 (/opt/reditools2/src/cineca/reditools.py) crashes with KeyError on IUPAC ambiguity bases (R,Y,S,W,K,M,B,D,H,V) because complement_map only defines A/T/C/G. complement() and complement_all() do a bare dict lookup, so any minus-strand read covering one of the ~150 ambiguity codes in GRCh38_no_alt_analysis_set kills the whole chromosome job.

Current workaround (option A, done): reditools_by_chrom in pipelines/Morales_et_al/rules/tools.smk now points -r at results/references/ref_iupac_masked.fasta (ambiguity codes -> N, which reditools already skips), built by the mask_iupac_in_reference rule. This loses those handful of positions.

Durable fix (option B): patch the REDItools2 Dockerfile (containers/reditools/) to extend complement_map with IUPAC complements (R<->Y, S<->S, W<->W, K<->M, B<->V, D<->H, N->N), rebuild reditools2.sif, then revert reditools_by_chrom back to the raw reference. REDItools v1 (REDItoolDnaRna.py comp()) already maps unknown bases to N and is unaffected.

CORRECTION on ML tool inputs (Morales_et_al pipeline, rules/tools.smk): redinet and red_ml are wired DIFFERENTLY. redinet (rule redinet, tools.smk:523) takes a REDItools outTable.gz as input (tools.smk:527) and classifies only those rows -> 100% subset of REDItools is CODE-ENFORCED via the reditools_redinet_by_chrom->join->bgzip chain (tools.smk:410+). red_ml (rule red_ml, tools.smk:240) takes only the rmdup BAM (tools.smk:242) and runs red_ML.pl --rnabam, doing its OWN detection then filtering by dbSNP/simpleRepeat/Alu/p-value; it is NOT constrained to REDItools candidates. The 81% red_ml-vs-reditools overlap is EMERGENT, not structural (3/16 red_ml sites fall outside reditools). Supersedes earlier claim that red_ml is structurally a reditools subset.

Permissivity verification (Morales_et_al_small, compare_all_tools matrices): site counts jacusa2=4848 > jacusa2_call1=1756 > reditools=1513 > bcftools=109 > red_ml=16 > sprint=14 > redinet=11. CLAIM 'JACUSA2 most permissive/sensitive' = VERIFIED (argmax volume; only 34% of its calls corroborated; jacusa2_call1 accepts ~100x lower edit fraction, median EF 0.0018 vs reditools 0.040). CLAIM 'SPRINT most stringent' = VERIFIED among de-novo callers (argmin of {jacusa2,jacusa2_call1,reditools,sprint}); redinet/red_ml are absolutely smaller but are downstream classifiers not de-novo callers. Summary doc: docs/consensus_permissivity_analysis.md; figures docs/figures/consensus_analysis/{consensus_vs_private,sprint_ml_dropout,tool_permissivity}.png

Why edit fractions differ across MARINE/REDItools3/SPRINT/JACUSA2_call1 (Morales_et_al, star aligner, Morales_et_al_small). THREE root causes: (1) coverage denominator differs - same 23 edited reads at chr12:6535556 gives frac 0.742 for reditools3/jacusa2 (cov 31) but 0.657 for MARINE (cov 35), identical evidence; (2) detection floors - min_coverage=5 wired into reditools3(-l)/jacusa2(-c) but NOT marine/sprint, so MARINE-only low-depth sites e.g. chr12:6344580 cov4 frac0.75; (3) reported quantity differs - reditools3=Frequency(2-decimal, rounds 1/711 to 0.00 -> NOT called), jacusa2_call1=LLR statistical score (flags 1/711=0.0014 as significant, chr21:25982458 same pileup 0,1,0,710 as reditools3 but opposite verdict), marine=count/coverage, sprint=supporting reads + NO fraction(always 0). Stats (star,6 clones): jacusa2_call1 1163 sites medCov3484 medFrac0.001; marine 849 sites medCov4668 medFrac0.0004 23.6% cov<5; reditools3 200 sites medCov27 medFrac0.05 0%cov<5 NO private sites (always co-called); sprint 14 sites medCov1(=support reads) frac0. SPRINT orthogonal (cluster/hyper-edit, not pileup). Parse logic in scripts/compare_all_tools.py: parse_sprint cov=supporting_reads frac=0 (res has no Freq col); parse_marine frac=count/coverage; parse_jacusa2_call1 frac=alt/sum(bases11) score=LLR. Doc: docs/edit_fraction_differences_across_tools.md
